comments.note: StandardRow::getValue(GridColumnInterface|string $column) returns the RegularCell object (not the raw scalar value), while the method name implies it returns the cell value. The SortManager correctly uses getCell($col)->getValue() to extract the scalar. This naming inconsistency (getValue returning a Cell vs a value) could confuse future developers. Consider renaming or adding a getScalarValue() method that returns the raw value directly.

SortManagerInterface does not expose sortRows(). The method is on the concrete SortManager but absent from the interface. Test code must use instanceof SortManager to call sortRows(), and DataGrid::generateOutput() accesses $this->sortManager directly (bypassing the interface). Adding sortRows() to SortManagerInterface would make the contract complete.

The test namespace in WP-004.md specifies AppUtils\Grids\Tests\Sorting, but all existing tests use AppUtils\Tests\{Module}. The actual test follows the real existing pattern (AppUtils\Tests\Sorting). The WP spec should be corrected for consistency.

comments.note: Callback sort mode is only tested for the default ASC direction. When sort_dir=DESC, the SortManager negates the callback's return value — this behavior is untested. A future test like test_callbackSorting_respectsDescDirection() would close this gap.

getSortURL() includes the raw path from $_SERVER['REQUEST_URI'] without sanitization. The output is safe to place in href attributes as HTTP query params are properly encoded via http_build_query(), but callers should still apply htmlspecialchars() when embedding the URL in HTML context to guard against XSS if REQUEST_URI is ever attacker-influenced.
No observation about code quality issues — implementation is clean, well-organized, and consistent with existing project conventions.

summary: Reviewed tests/Sorting/ColumnSortingTest.php and examples/4-pagination.php against all four review dimensions (maintainability, best practices, security/performance, future context).
All 18 test methods are well-scoped, readable, and follow established project patterns (setUp/tearDown superglobal management mirrors ArrayPaginationTest/GridPaginationTest).

Renderer uses HTMLTag::attr() to set sort URLs — HTML attribute escaping is handled by the library; no raw string interpolation into HTML output. getSortURL() safely handles parse_url() edge cases (falls back to '/' on missing REQUEST_URI; path-only extraction prevents javascript: scheme injection).

No blocking issues identified. All pre-existing design observations (sortRows() missing from interface, concrete SortManager cast in DataGrid::generateOutput()) are tracked debt, not introduced by this WP.
examples/4-pagination.php cleanly demonstrates useNativeSorting() on two columns with the fluent API, consistent with project conventions. PASS.

comments.note: SortManagerInterface does not declare sortRows(). Tests work around this with `instanceof SortManager` cast; DataGrid::generateOutput() also accesses $this->sortManager at the concrete type. Adding sortRows(array &$rows): void to SortManagerInterface would complete the contract and eliminate the cast in both places. Pre-existing debt, not introduced by WP-004.

Callback sorting with SORT_DESC direction is untested. SortManager::sortRows() negates the callback result when $dir === SORT_DESC, which could produce counter-intuitive double-negation behavior if the callback itself reverses order. A test_callbackSorting_respectsDescDirection() test would document and validate this behavior.

WP-004 spec specified namespace AppUtils\Grids\Tests\Sorting, but the actual test (correctly) uses AppUtils\Tests\Sorting to match all existing test files. The WP spec contained an error; the implementation is correct. The spec document should be updated for future reference.

getSortURL() is currently consumed only via HTMLTag::attr(), which handles HTML entity escaping. Any future caller that echoes the return value directly into HTML template strings (outside HTMLTag) must apply htmlspecialchars(). Consider adding a @return string annotation note, or an internal helper URL-encode step on the path segment, to make this explicit for future developers.
